faces.f: Though they had never left the Core, the Oltec knew the stars.
"There's a whole world under the surface, waiting for the light of our salvation."
Whatever the tide brings in, the shapers can wash away.
"With each sacrifice, we step closer to the Age of Everflowing Blood."
When they ran short on cannonballs, they went for the pots and pans.
They gulp down their prey on the run, claws dripping with blood as they hunt for their next meal.
After long days of squeezing through cramped tunnels, the Sun Empire's dinosaurs were overjoyed to stretch their necks and survey the wonders of the Core.
"The language of the Komon Winaq has much in common with the tongue of our ancestors. Surely the two peoples once lived and worked in close harmony."
The Oltec revere dinosaurs as living remnants of the bygone Fourth Age.
With a flare of plumage and an earthshaking bellow, it can scare off predators three times its size.
"Good thing I'm not afraid of heights."
"Like water between rivers, wisdom must flow freely from one generation to the next."
"There's a whole world under the surface, waiting for the light of our salvation."
Whatever the tide brings in, the shapers can wash away.
"With each sacrifice, we step closer to the Age of Everflowing Blood."
When they ran short on cannonballs, they went for the pots and pans.
They gulp down their prey on the run, claws dripping with blood as they hunt for their next meal.

"Good thing I'm not afraid of heights."
"Like water between rivers, wisdom must flow freely from one generation to the next."

"Everyone is obsessed with this cosmium stuff, but I can sense some kind of comparable power in this droplet of ancient amber."
—Quintorius Kand, research notes

"Markings on the hilt are faded, but resemble Komon Winaq familial glyphs. Relic recovered for further study."
—Oltec archaeological survey

"The rose is common in Legion heraldry. Thorns and petals tell of specific family achievements."
—Quintorius Kand, research notes

"Relic retrieval is delayed. Mentioning it was forty feet tall might have helped us prepare."
—Queen's Bay Company dispatch

"Oltec maps are not simple charts of place and distance. Each tells a story of exploration and learning, celebrating the meaning beyond the discovery."
—Huatli's travel journal

"Willem put it on and started shooting sparks from his hands like some kind of wizard! Was supposed to be my turn next, but the blasted thing won't come off his hand. Send help."
—Brazen Coalition expedition dispatch

"Skim all the gold and magic rocks you want, but if I see one greasy fingerprint on my new boots, you'll be drinking bilgewater for a month."
—Note from Captain Lannery Storm

"Akal theorizes that it is some sort of signal, resonating beyond this cavern's physical space. But if so, who—or what—is the signal for?"
—Huatli's travel journal

"Bells ring out to mark every great moment in the Malamet's tale of years: victories and tragedies, feasts and discoveries, the ascension of each sovereign and their passage into the dark beyond."
—Sun Empire expedition report

"The artifact's interaction with the mycoid network seems to allow non-mycoids to connect to the gestalt consciousness. Thus far, all who have done so have fled screaming."
—Alvaro, Dusk Legion researcher

"It bends the light somehow, rendering it—and its wearer—functionally invisible. I never would have found it if I hadn't tripped over it!"
—Quintorius Kand, research notes

"The strange energy source isn't cosmium after all, but some unidentifiable material that has leached cosmium residue from the walls. Could be dangerous. Could change everything."
—Oltec archaeological survey
Its roaring challenge is punctuated by the slam of its tail on the earth, rousing the herds of the plains.
The best presents are impossible to regift.

"There are moments when I feel I could fly like the sunwing. Far away I would soar, but always a golden gale pushes me back."
—Huatli

"Its rise is like the sun's, a beautiful beginning. Its descent is like the sun's, a frightful ending."
—Huatli
"Should I fall, take up our standard and carry on. The Legion must always prevail."
In the rapture of his Blood Fast, he destroyed the navigator's tools and steered the ship to shore by faith alone.
Some timelines forever fray, branch, and intermingle. Others end abruptly.
"The arc of my blade has carved a path of light for the peace that will follow."

"Kinjalli sculpted humans from clay, but the dinosaurs were carved from unyielding stone."
—Itzama the Crested

"Kinjalli's encompassing rays herald new life in the moment of the sun's dawning."
—Chitlati, Lightning Rider
From the moment they arrived, wedding guests were met with a pageant of wealth and excess.
The sky takes flight and the earth trembles.
"You can come back once you've learned some manners—and figured out how to reconstitute your physical forms."

"Your concern for my safety is touching, but as long as your gunners remain reliably erratic, I see no reason to change course."
—Admiral Yelise, to Commodore Axurik
"I am my life's work."
The wills of mortals shift as the tide ebbs and flows.
"Lungs full of sea air and a hold full of loot. Ah, what a life!"
Another imminent battle subsided in busy snuffling and carefree rooting.
"They'll never see me coming."
A visit to the Deeproot Tree and its ancient spring replenishes a merfolk's connection to nature.
Even before Teferi heard Wrenn's call, a few Zhalfirins were roused from sleep by a strange, otherworldly song.

"Abandon ship! No, grab the treasure first!"
—Admiral Beckett Brass
"You might as well try to stop the waterfall."
Few things are truly "lost" at sea.
"I know these waters better than you know yourselves."
"Let the land dwellers know the coast is no longer the border between our realms. A new age of empire has begun."
"Tell you what, you keep the rope."
"Be like the sea: flow around that which is unmovable; for everything else, crash into it unrelentingly."
Steady and silent as the deep current, the reejerey guides the course of the school.

"We've merged your life essence with that of several creatures at once. You're welcome."
—Speaker Trifon
The masks float downstream toward the Mirrorlake, where faces arise to wear them.
Where the light falls dim and blue on broken ships, secrets lie unclaimed.
He's the calm that hides the coming storm.

"Any ship that sails on these mean seas for long is bound to pick up a ghost or two."
—Admiral Beckett Brass
Made from trout scales and crawfish whiskers, merrows' shimmering banners flash in the water like lightning.
They ride on waves of aether, washing out anything that might pollute the Merrow Lanes.

"To fill your mind with knowledge, we must start by emptying it."
—Barrin, master wizard

"Vanya Falkenrath's paintings are astonishing. How does she manage to achieve such rich crimson hues?"
—Stefan, art critic
The more you have, the more you have to lose.
"The veil of death hides little from our kind."
"Flee all you like. The further you run the more firmly I feel your heartbeat."
His verdict is always guilty. His sentence is always death.
"Drench these golden streets in the blood of our enemies."
"Please, come in! Hors d'oeuvres are on the table."
"Lady Anje said no violence at the wedding. She never said anything about the journey there!"
His fists fume with the decay of death, each strike a plague on the hearts of his enemies.
"I will not live as a slave. If you would be free, then fight alongside me."
Once they reached Orazca, the Legion's explorers ransacked tombs and temples, hunting for the Immortal Sun.
Even as humans regained the upper hand, some still willingly traded their lives for a chance at immortality.
"I often think on how excited they must feel to be chosen as my prey."
"Join me, and take the world for yourself!"

"On vile wings and bloody wind, the swarm will rise."
—Skyclave inscription
"If you're not surrounded by decadence, my question to you is—why not?"

"Now isn't that better?"
—Olivia Voldaren
Under Drana's leadership, vampires are finding new strength in unity.

"My conquistadors are never slain, merely laid to rest."
—Queen Miralda the Pious

"These worthless cattle think they can sneak unnoticed into my wedding? Dispose of them."
—Olivia Voldaren
"Our quarrels behind us. Our foes before us. Death or triumph for us all!"
"Shame to let good gold go to the grave."
The Sanctum Seekers were the first of the knightly orders to cross the sea and are still the most zealous.
The Skelle raise scorn poles in conquered villages—cursed effigies of wood and bone that sap survivors of physical strength and the will to fight back.
In matters of life and death, he trusts his gut.
"The time for subtlety is over, darling."
Captain Angrath cares less about treasure than mayhem. If he can't leave Ixalan, he'll burn the plane down.

"Holy places are no longer sanctuary from death, and death is no longer sanctuary from anything."
—Thalia, Knight-Cathar
"We sail. We plunder. Then we dance."
In the moment before her execution, she realized what it meant to be a pyromancer, to be alive, to be Chandra.
"Choose, vampire: our hat on your head, or no hat, no head."
The storm rages and the earth breaks.
Aboard her ship, the *Dragon's Smile*, Kari follows no one's rules but her own.

"Stand still and try not to look like prey!"
—Skerk Hobnett, wilderness guide
"Forward! Let the Burning Sun's light guide you to deserving prey!"
"Smash and grab, loot and burn, then it is the next town's turn!"

"It is the nature of souls that they burn more brightly together than apart."
—Vessifrus, flamekin demagogue
It brings belligerence to new heights.

"Monsters dwell in every heart. We only think civilization tames them."
—Euphemia, Nexus watcher
As Aclazotz's undead forces approached the temple of Ojer Kaslem, they met a roaring wall of vibrant, flourishing life.
All seeds share a common bond, calling to each other across infinity.
"You think I stand alone? I have the forest at my call, the waters at my back. I outnumber you."
"I do not lead. They do not follow. We walk together."
"To care for yourself, cultivate the world. To care for the world, cultivate yourself."
An explorer's reward is a view of tomorrow's possibilities.
Her song twines throughout the Core, a melodic message to all Oltec near and far: you are home.

"Naga shed their scales. We wear ours with pride."
—Golran, dragonscale captain
"Now is the hour. Ours is the duty. For victory and family—charge!"

"The land grows only where the kami will it."
—Dosan the Falling Leaf
Not even the tallest tree stands a chance against the underside of a dinosaur's foot.
Nature grows solutions to its problems.
They cover their territory like a tide of teeth and claws.
"The curse is broken."
Raptors are clever enough to tear away a hard metal shell to get at the tasty morsel inside.
"Control the Great Conduit? You might as well try to divert a river with your hands."
The gourd carving was supposed to take place *after* the feast.
The Sun Empire's most sacred sites are protected by more than prayers.
The herds follow as new growth arises.

"It appears that nature has risen against us."
—Captain Brinely Rage

"Ixalli's fertile rays enliven us all. Each of us is a testament to the sun's strength and love."
—Chitlati, Lightning Rider
"You and your ship will make a fine addition to my fleet."
Streams of gold and bright feathers flash in the orb, visions of past and future.
She follows the old tributaries built when merrows still shaped the tides.
"Whichever side wins, I'm sure the banquet will be superb."
Her centuries-long search is ended.
Cyclical and spiral patterns are the specialty of the Gyre Clade, which seeks to revitalize the cycles of nature.

faces.chapters:
(As this Saga enters and after your draw step, add a lore counter. Sacrifice after III.)
I — Each player mills four cards. Then you may exile a creature or planeswalker card from each graveyard.
II, III — Until end of turn, you may cast spells from among cards exiled with this Saga, and you may spend mana as though it were mana of any color to cast those spells.

faces.f: "She may call herself Kiora but I believe she is Thassa, the embodiment of the sea and empress of the depths."
"We long ago abandoned the things that make humans weak: friendship, marriage, family. All that remains is the strength of our devotion."

"The mist clothes us when we are bare, hides us when we are alone, and unites us when we are together."
—Nirit of Pashona's band
Its breath is a gale. Its roar is a volcano. Its anger tears soul from flesh.
Carnivorous dinosaurs developed a taste for undead flesh, tracking the vampires by the scent of blood on their breath.

"Let all feel joy in pain."
—Rakdos

"Seeing a pack of these monsters hunt together, I'm at a loss to imagine the size of their prey."
—Adrian Adanto of Lujio
Some view Domri's unlikely ascent as a sign of Ilharg the Raze-Boar's imminent return.
"Yavimaya is one being—one vastness of rippling leaves, one deepness of roots, and one chatter of animals—of which I am one part."

"I came seeking a challenge. All I found was you."
—Zurgo, khan of the Mardu
"For four hundred years, I have led armies of conquest. These lands hold nothing that can stand against me."
"I used to hurl rocks and eat scraps of meat burned over a fire. Look at what I've become and tell me Simic does not hold infinite possibility."
It started as a mere drop of water. The Magic Mirror crystallized it into much more.
It harmonizes with the essence of its master.
An emblem of a secret guild, the Dimir insignia is seen only by its own members—and the doomed.
The Izzet signet is redesigned often, each time becoming closer to a vanity portrait of Niv-Mizzet.

"Inspiration is found by looking outward."
—Oviya Pashiri, sage lifecrafter

"We have barely begun to learn the secrets of the Fourth People. Every remnant of their presence, however cryptic, is a gift."
—Akal Pakal, First Steward of Oteclan
The sigil holds different meanings depending on its form and presentation. While some wear it as a sign of status, others wear it as a sign of debt.
Made of bone and boiled in blood, a Rakdos signet is not considered finished until it has been used as a murder weapon.

For the Simic Combine, its sigil serves not as an emblem of honor but as a trademark. Its familiar image on any biological commodity attests to superb craftsmanship, ingenious innovation, and higher cost.
Lost to time is the artificer's art of trapping light from a distant star in a ring of purest gold.

"There is great wisdom in rushing headlong into combat . . . if you're prepared."
—Kenjek, captain of the Thousand Swords

"You'll never get to the top if you don't know who's already there."
—Kaya
"It is said Chimil never sees the same lands twice. So too must we expand our horizons."
Persecuted alchemists fled deep into Kessig's wilds, seeking solitude to continue their ghoulish craft.
Chuuy Kaaj, "The Hanging City," has endured for centuries as the thriving hub of Malamet art, life, and culture.
On the volcanic continent of Akoum, bizarre vegetation clusters around gas vents, and jagged mountain peaks rise high into the air.
Oteclan, the Oltec capital, encompasses diverse satellite cities. The Oltec can live in any environment and maintain connection.

"Approach my tower on bended knee or depart from it as ash upon the wind."
—Gadwick, the Wizened
It's said the spirits of the drowned dead hang their lights from the shattered figureheads.
A lonely sentinel facing gales, hurricanes, and tides of homicidal spirits.
The Sun Empire bends nature— rivers, mountainsides, dinosaurs—to its unyielding will.

"It was a strange morning. When we awoke, we found our trees transformed. We didn't know whether to water them or polish them."
—Pulan, Bant orchardist
A smoldering storm of chilling fire.
A seething locus of reverent rage.
All are welcome.

"Our ancestors brought down a Phyrexian portal ship, then built our town on its hull. We're pretty proud of that."
—Alene of Riverspan
Serra's blessing lies strongest upon Sursi, where her holy chapels are untouched even as evil encroaches.
The people of the Sun Empire worship the sun in three aspects: the creative sun, the sustaining sun, and the destructive sun.

"I can't protect everyone here. But those I can, I will."
—Karn
When a werewolf changes for the first time, that first howl is said to echo through the wilds till moonset.

"Some see a coastal disaster. I see a fully-stocked seagraf."
—Jadar, ghoulcaller of Nephalia
Once guarded by the Knights of the Reliquary, the tower stands now protected only by its own remoteness, its dusty treasures open to plunder by anyone.
Rumors quickly spread among thieves about a labyrinth without walls and a prize beyond all measures of worth.
A flickering beacon of righteous corruption.
The continent of Guul Draz is a geothermal swampland reeking of heat and decay.
Skirsdag cultists meet behind a waterfall's curtain and plot with demonic forces.
On the continent of Tazeem, rushing waters plunge through narrow canyons into mist-cloaked lakes.

"When gods become apathetic, the people will worship anyone who answers their pleas."
—Kiora
Take two steps north into the unsettled future, south into the unquiet past, east into the present day, or west into the great unknown.
As eons passed, the rock wore away, revealing the rich colors at the mountain's heart.
Far from human eyes, birds flit between vivid blossoms in a hidden paradise.
Wildflowers here bloom not with the season but with the ebb and flow of magic.
All the wonders of the natural world in one breathtaking microcosm.
Beauty appears in strange places for those with eyes to see it.

"For centuries my creation kept this world in balance. Now only her shadow remains."
—Sorin Markov
A verdant paradox of primal logic.
Quintorius touched the old poncho he'd found. A rush of magic condensed into an Echo, and wise Abuelo stepped forth.
As the cliff began to crumble, Wayta danced fearlessly across the tumbling stones, knowing Ajij would never let her fall.
Left to their own devices, gnomes reengineer their own devices.
Few humans are steady-handed enough to match a gnome's precision. Even the slightest change to a single line can wildly alter a glyph's meaning.

"I love the smell of freshly baked gnomes!"
—Yelha, Oltec artisan
Cosmium is the tangible essence of Chimil's power. The Oltec's cosmium-laced tattoos ensure that power can be called upon when needed.
To their dismay, Brazen Coalition explorers soon found that the Oltec were not impressed by cannons.

"All that is made can be unmade. Chimil's light is the only constant."
—Oltec artificers' creed
Though wary of each other at first, the Malamet and the Oltec found a common enemy in the mycoids. They began to share glyph knowledge and other crafting secrets.
Huatli smiled up at Akal. "Our peoples have too long been parted, and yet we are cousins still."
"Everyone wants to be remembered. Few are willing to do what it takes."
The Core was sealed long ago by the Deep Gods, who set the angels to the eternal task of defending its golden gates.
Itzmin walked away from the collapse with a new friend—and an enduring fear of heights.

"Train your mind and your muscles with equal ferocity, cub. Without wisdom, even a mighty warrior is nothing but a bully."
—Sovereign Okinec Ahau
The glyph is mightier than the sword.
"Maize, sweet and fresh! Tamal, hot and filling! Water, still or sparkling!"
Malamet histories speak of a time when they were not yet confined to mortal bodies and existed as ferocity unrestrained.

"Either he made a gnome very angry when he took that, or he'll make one very happy when he brings it back."
—Ihio, Oteclan market vendor

n: Ojer Taq, Deepest Foundation // Temple of Civilization

faces.f: Chimil gave the Oltec life. Ojer Taq taught them how to live together.
Many Oltec youth dream of one day joining the elite bat-riding cavalry of the Thousand Moons military force.
Dusk Legion invaders sought lone Oltec travelers to prey upon. The Core's guidestones did not approve.
Those who break the laws of the Malamet become cold, silent warnings to others who might try.

"Those who would steal the blood and breath of the living will drink their fill of the sand."
—Sovereign Okinec Ahau

"Look! Aclazotz sends his children to watch over our pilgrimage."
—Clavileño, First of the Blessed
"Fang-brethren, we feed together."
The Thousand Moons practice every maneuver thousands of times, allowing them to strike flawlessly without hesitation in the heat of battle.
The Thousand Moons train and fight in tight-knit squads of ten. Every tenth Moon functions as an officer, every hundredth as a captain, and the thousandth, Anim Pakal, as supreme commander.

n: Thousand Moons Smithy // Barracks of the Thousand

faces.f: Never leave home without a gnome.
"No one soul is worth more than Torrezon's salvation. Press on."
"These lost children of Aclazotz are misguided, but perhaps there can be reconciliation of our ideals without war."
A typical conversation with Echoes is three parts wisdom and one part gossip.
When the Malamet told him to avoid the river, he thought they meant it wasn't safe to drink.
The Oltec repurpose objects out of reverence rather than scarcity, believing them strengthened by the memory of each past function.
As the River Heralds began to decipher the ancient map, they were staggered by the vastness of the world-within-the-world that it revealed.
Years of adventure and adversity on the open seas did not prepare Brog for the humiliation of losing a sparring match to a cogwork doll less than half his size.
Explorers learned not to tamper with sites of ancient power without learning their purpose.
The Komon Winaq, ancestors of the Oltec, linger on as the eldest of the Echoes.
"These glyphs are more than trail markings! They tell a story as they go. But does it end in celebration or tragedy?"
The folk of the Sun Empire respect their ancestors. The Oltec go further, communing with spirits of esteemed elders after death.
It is ill-advised to swim where even the River Heralds do not.

n: The Enigma Jewel // Locus of Enlightenment
The Everflowing Well // The Myriad Pools

faces.f:
"Remember that weird salamander thing we found in the jungle stream? I think we just met its god."
—Carella, quartermaster of the *Windshark*
It devoured the shell's original owner long ago, but it's just about ready to start looking for a new home—and a meal to go with it.
The force of a blizzard. The rage of a monstrosaur.
Ancient glyphs are a lot harder to decipher when attached to an apex predator.

"Learn all you can of this underground sea. I suspect more secrets of our ancestors lie waiting in its depths."
—Tishana
The ship's carpenter adorned the figurehead with a small cosmium gem, never expecting the figurehead to take flight.

n: Ojer Pakpatiq, Deepest Epoch // Temple of Cyclical Time

faces.f: Chimil gave the Oltec time. Ojer Pakpatiq gave them the tools to learn its lessons.
Between Quintorius's archaeological expertise and Huatli's knowledge of ancient glyphs, the "impossible" lock finally yielded, and the door to the underground world rumbled open.

"The Core is not a simple trove to be plundered by intruders from the surface. It will reject those who do not accord it respect."
—Akal Pakal, First Steward of Oteclan
"Landlubbers just don't understand the value of a proper hat."

"Well, that's one less share to divide up."
—Dranach, Dire Fleet boatswain
"Don't worry, little swimmers. I'm here for the ruins, not you."
"After this age, another."
Some Echoes remember every moment of their past lives and spend their existence contemplating past choices.
"That's close enough, stranger."
"Leave you? Not a chance. You still owe me money."

"First rule down here is the same as it is on the water: always double-check your knots."
—Captain Lannery Storm
"The only drink in your future is seawater."
Its kin once overran entire civilizations, but they tore each other to pieces in their unending hunger. Now only it remains.

n: Aclazotz, Deepest Betrayal // Temple of the Dead

faces.f: Chimil gave the Oltec peace in death. Aclazotz ripped it away.
"Great Aclazotz, receive this offering. Wrought with skill. Captured with strength. Anointed with the blood of your enemies."
The pull of duty was so strong that they barely paused to notice they'd died.
Though he wept at Inti's death, Caparocti's eyes were keen, and his spear pierced cleanly through Clavileño's tainted heart.
Its very presence rips old wounds open to bleed anew.

"This weapon embodies both the strength and the weakness of the Legion of Dusk. They will endure any pain to achieve their ends, but they suffer pointlessly just to prove their dedication."
—Huatli
As the massive mycoids known as rage titans charge into battle, lesser ones swarm in their wake, gobbling up any survivors.
It needs no food, yet still it hungers.
The hired goblins were not, as advertised, worth their weight in gold.
Mycoids have no concept of life or death. All things exist, and all things can be made useful.
"Go away! I found it first!"
The first shriek locates the prey. The second immobilizes it.

"It's a mournful fate, to remember so well the taste of blood yet be forever unable to drink."
—Bartolomé del Presidio, director of the Queen's Bay Company
The gateway could be opened only by the spilling of innocent blood. Vito did not hesitate.

"Does *everything* down here want to suck my blood?"
—Derilene, expedition porter
The shadows make no mark upon the flesh. It is the mind they claw and strangle.
Neither Nurgam nor the mycoid who laid the trap could quite believe their luck.
The more creatures that plunge to their deaths in the abyss, the more angry Echoes that arise to drag others down.
Aclazotz laughed as the dark shards closed around Chimil, plunging the Core into unnatural darkness. At long last, his bloody reign would begin.

"Don't look at me. I'm not drinking it."
—Dranach, Dire Fleet boatswain
Cave crawlers devour anything from plant matter to solid rock, but they prefer fresh meat.

"We know Chimil's light as a warming, healing presence, but make no mistake: to those who would desecrate her lands, it is a terrible force of scouring fury."
—Akal Pakal, First Steward of Oteclan
After a slow death in darkness, she flies into a rage at the slightest glimpse of light.

"Oh, come on! Aren't regular snails gross enough?"
—Derilene, expedition porter

"As the snake sheds its skin to be born anew, we cast off death to rise as servants of Aclazotz."
—Vito, Church of Dusk heretic
"Do you remember us?"
Caverns uninhabited by mycoids are often infested with worse.

"It's no good killing them? Then what do we do? Distract them with a tea party?"
—Mervin, Brazen Coalition prospector

n: Tarrian's Journal // The Tomb of Aclazotz

faces.f: Though officially deemed a heretic for his reverent writings on Aclazotz, Tarrian is viewed as a holy martyr by the most radical sects of the Church of Dusk.
Those who go under rise again as cruel mockeries of their former selves, spewing foul water and keening with sorrow.

"Slake my thirst so that we both may be free."
—Faded inscription

"It's not my fault! The glyphs for 'blessed' and 'cursed' look very similar!"
—Diego, Brazen Coalition translator
"We usher in the Age of Everflowing Blood, when those who are fed upon will be fed, and those who feed will be satiated."

"What do you mean a walking clock destroyed all our cannons?!"
—Captain Lannery Storm

"You surface-dwellers may have forgotten your history, but it has not forgotten you."
—Akal Pakal, First Steward of Oteclan
One day it will be as terrifying as it thinks it is.

n: Brass's Tunnel-Grinder // Tecutlan, the Searing Rift

faces.f: "The secret is footwork. Plus an extra sword."
"By fire and lightning, tooth and claw, we will send these invaders fleeing back to Torrezon!"

"For 'immortal conquerors,' these vampires seem very susceptible to being crushed by boulders."
—Chara Rebal, bat rider
It is a living eruption, unquenchable fury given form.
"Put your hammers away and bring me some blankets! Such a gift from Tilonalli must be handled with the utmost care."

"Oh, Saheeli would *love* you."
—Huatli
"Thought you were out of my skull-bashin' range, didn't you?"

"A little innovation can lead to a big score."
—Admiral Beckett Brass

"That's the fifth ship lost in three days! Can't we build them out of something stronger?"
—Malcolm Lee
"He would've wanted me to have it!"
Enterprising goblins can extract their body weight in loot. Ambitious ones have a big meal first.

"Let's send our vampiric visitors a welcoming party, shall we?"
—Anim Pakal, Thousandth Moon
As the surface-dwellers became bolder in their intrusions, Oltec artificers began to repurpose courier gnomes for intelligence gathering and distraction.

n: Idol of the Deep King // Sovereign's Macuahuitl
Ojer Axonil, Deepest Might // Temple of Power

faces.f: Chimil gave the Oltec passion. Ojer Axonil challenged them to harness it.
Early Sun Empire expeditions learned the hard way that some surface dinosaurs were particularly ill-suited to the caverns' enclosed environments.
"Whatever it is, it set off a trap. It must be valuable!"
"You inspire me."
Anticipating tight spaces and trivial fauna, the first Dusk Legion expeditions were small, mobile, and lightly armored. Hundreds of casualties later, they started sending plate-clad platoons.
Sometimes an expedition reaches a natural conclusion. Sometimes it all just comes crashing down.
While Huatli ventured underground, Saheeli used her unique expertise to bolster the Sun Empire's defenses.

"She's a smart one. Noticed all on her own that the bloodsuckers wave their hands around to do their filthy magic, so she rips off their hands first."
—Citamitzin, Sun Empire warrior
"Let Tilonalli's light burn a path through this darkness."
As the Legion of Dusk closed in, Oltec citizens rallied to support the Thousand Moons and drive off the invaders.

"The ground is on fire, the ceiling's made of spears, and I think a mushroom tried to curse me. Don't tell me not to panic!"
—Jino Grag, Brazen Coalition scout
With crunchy outer shells and juicy innards, cave crawlers quickly became a favorite snack of the Sun Empire's dinosaur companions.
Touched eons ago by Ojer Axonil's flaming macuahuitl, it still burns with his boundless fury.

"She's devoted to protecting her herd. We're just lucky she considers us part of it."
—Huatli

"Even our most learned philosophers can only hope to approach the inner serenity of the humble capybara."
—Nelli, Oltec didact
Many temples have strong foundations. Few are also wise.
"If you're afraid to dive into the unknown, how will you ever find anything new?"
The difference between trash and treasure is a matter of perspective.
Accustomed to hunting nimble flying prey, the dinosaur was delighted to have its meal delivered neatly in a box.
"I'm telling you, the wall just blinked!"

"I suggest we leave this cavern for someone else to conquer."
—Amalia, master cartographer
A thundering roar calls forth a primeval army.

"Wow. It's a good thing we brought a poet."
—Wayta

n: Growing Rites of Itlimoc // Itlimoc, Cradle of the Sun

faces.f: Though the Sun Empire and the River Heralds once came together to plant the sacred forest, its roots have been tended by the mycoids ever since.

n: Huatli, Poet of Unity // Roar of the Fifth People

faces.chapters:
(As this Saga enters and after your draw step, add a lore counter. Sacrifice after IV.)
I — Create two 3/3 green Dinosaur creature tokens.
II — This Saga gains "Creatures you control have '{T}: Add {R}, {G}, or {W}.'"
III — Search your library for a Dinosaur card, reveal it, put it into your hand, then shuffle.
IV — Dinosaurs you control gain double strike and trample until end of turn.

faces.f:
"Inti's name will grace our poems and histories for generations. Yours will collect dust, forgotten, in this cave."
—Huatli, to Vito

"I watched him rip a Phyrexian dreadnought in half once. A few vampires will barely slow him down."
—Huatli

"Finally, those glowing purple bone-monsters are gone and we can get back to the real excitement: archaeology!"
—Quintorius Kand
"Did we follow the dinosaurs out of the caverns, or did they follow us? These glyphs could change our entire understanding of our history."
When the merfolk fled underground, they brought the life force of the jungle with them.
The River Heralds found clues to a grand heritage below Ixalan's surface.
The Oltec long ago abandoned the caverns to the mycoids, but the Deep Gods still keep watch over the spore-strewn darkness.

"Let's not give the surface-dwellers time to learn what tactics work best here."
—Daram, Malamet marshal
"I bear the marking of the Deep King, and in his name I will rend you to nothing but spores on the wind!"
The mightiest Malamet warriors train as titan-killers, elite champions capable of facing down the caverns' most fearsome beasts.
Anything that falls into the pit—relics, rubble, even corpses—ends up snared in its magic-infused web.

n: Ojer Kaslem, Deepest Growth // Temple of Cultivation

faces.f: Chimil gave the Oltec sacred lands. Ojer Kaslem brought them to life.
When you don't know what dangers you'll face, bring the biggest danger with you.

"Bright as any dinosaur—and just as with other great hunters, its colors are a warning."
—Huatli

"I don't know whether it hates the mycoids or just loves breaking things. I say we leave it be."
—Samin, Oltec scout
"We weren't fleeing a broken world. We were running toward paradise!"
"Halt, traveler. Whatever you seek, you will not find it here."

"Ah well... the temple was due for a new roof anyhow."
—Kusi, Oltec gardener
Every mycoid carries within itself the makings of an entire colony.

"I suppose we'll just hope those ancient monoliths lost to our people for centuries weren't particularly important."
—Toxayac, Sun Empire historian
"Come, friends. Let us see if this world remembers us."
"If we are to protect this world, we can no longer hide within it!"
"Bless this sinner, who sacrificed his blood so that I may live."
"To the mother lode, and death take the wary!"

"Dinosaurs have no concept of royalty, but they recognize the scent of the mightiest among them."
—Atla Palani, nest tender
"Invaders in the West Chasm? Give me an hour and they'll be fungus food."

"The Fomori are a foul and distant memory, but their war machines taught us much about large-scale armorcraft."
—Anim Pakal, Thousandth Moon
"This water can guide you anywhere, if you know how to ask."
What began as a single gift for Huatli became a battalion of automatons unlike anything ever seen on Ixalan.
As surface empires send their explorers down, his hungry eyes look upward.
Due to archaic Brazen Coalition guidelines regarding hats, a few mycoids are now technically pirate captains.
Ever since the Fomori's attempt long ago to extinguish Chimil's light, the Oltec have taken extensive measures to never get lost in the Core.

"I'm certain it's some kind of sophisticated navigational tool. If only I had any idea what it was telling me!"
—Colbo, Brazen Coalition surveyor
Wherever the spores begin to take hold, it crushes the ground to rubble.
They scour for secrets in places too distant or dangerous for humans to tread.

"Ow! I think a wasp just stung me, cap'n."
—Nirk Doobin, last words

n: Matzalantli, the Great Door // The Core

faces.f: Centuries ago, under siege from the Mycotyrant, the Oltec sealed the Core off from the world... until Huatli's party arrived.
"Run, hearties, run! Or we'll end our days as pirate paste!"
It knows the length, pitch, and orientation of every tunnel it has ever traversed.
Tarrian's holy weapon still holds a fragment of his dark power... and his hunger.

n: Throne of the Grim Captain // The Grim Captain

faces.f: Many footprints lead into the cave. None lead out.
The still, silent waters reflect what was, not what is.
The Komon Winaq left behind few written records, but their handiwork stands strong all throughout the Core.
United under the banner of the Brazen Coalition, pirates put aside their feuds to plunder the underground bounty.

n: Huatli, Poet of Unity // Roar of the Fifth People

faces.f: Quintorius touched the old poncho he'd found. A rush of magic condensed into an Echo, and wise Abuelo stepped forth.
"Fang-brethren, we feed together."

n: Thousand Moons Smithy // Barracks of the Thousand

faces.f: The Oltec repurpose objects out of reverence rather than scarcity, believing them strengthened by the memory of each past function.
"These glyphs are more than trail markings! They tell a story as they go. But does it end in celebration or tragedy?"

n: The Enigma Jewel // Locus of Enlightenment
The Everflowing Well // The Myriad Pools

faces.f: "Do you remember us?"

n: Tarrian's Journal // The Tomb of Aclazotz

faces.f: Though officially deemed a heretic for his reverent writings on Aclazotz, Tarrian is viewed as a holy martyr by the most radical sects of the Church of Dusk.
Those who go under rise again as cruel mockeries of their former selves, spewing foul water and keening with sorrow.

n: Brass's Tunnel-Grinder // Tecutlan, the Searing Rift

faces.f: "Thought you were out of my skull-bashin' range, didn't you?"
"You inspire me."
Many temples have strong foundations. Few are also wise.

n: Growing Rites of Itlimoc // Itlimoc, Cradle of the Sun

faces.f: Though the Sun Empire and the River Heralds once came together to plant the sacred forest, its roots have been tended by the mycoids ever since.
The River Heralds found clues to a grand heritage below Ixalan's surface.
"Halt, traveler. Whatever you seek, you will not find it here."
Due to archaic Brazen Coalition guidelines regarding hats, a few mycoids are now technically pirate captains.

n: Matzalantli, the Great Door // The Core

faces.f: Centuries ago, under siege from the Mycotyrant, the Oltec sealed the Core off from the world... until Huatli's party arrived.
Tarrian's holy weapon still holds a fragment of his dark power... and his hunger.
Benalia has a complex caste system that changes with the lunar year. No matter what the season, the only caste that cannot be attained by either heredity or money is that of the hero.

Before a woman marries in the village of Sursi, she must visit the land of the Mesa Pegasus. Legend has it that if the woman is pure of heart and her love is true, a Mesa Pegasus will appear, blessing her family with long life and good fortune.

"Look to the north; there you will find aid and comfort."
—The Book of Tal

"'Do you know, I always thought Unicorns were fabulous monsters, too? I never saw one alive before!' 'Well, now that we have seen each other,' said the Unicorn, 'if you'll believe in me, I'll believe in you.'" —Lewis Carroll
Healers ultimately acquire the divine gifts of spiritual and physical wholeness. The most devout are also granted the ability to pass physical wholeness on to others.

The traditional kings of the jungle command a healthy respect in other climates as well. Relying mainly on their stealth and speed, Savannah Lions can take a victim by surprise, even in the endless flat plains of their homeland.
Born with wings of light and a sword of faith, this heavenly incarnation embodies both fury and purity.
Good bodyguards are hard to find, mainly because they don't live long.

Just as the evil ones approached to slay Justina, she cast a great spell, imbuing her weapons with her own life force. Thus she fulfilled the prophecy: "In the death of your savior will you find salvation."
Out of the blackness and stench of the engulfing swamp emerged a shimmering figure. Only the splattered armor and ichor-stained sword hinted at the unfathomable evil the knight had just laid waste.
These spirits of the air are winsome and wild, and cannot be truly contained. Only marginally intelligent, they often substitute whimsy for strategy, delighting in mischief and mayhem.
A master of tactics, the Lord of Atlantis makes his people bold in battle merely by arriving to lead them.
Of royal blood among the spirits of the air, the Mahamoti Djinn rides on the wings of the winds. As dangerous in the gambling hall as he is in battle, he is a master of trickery and misdirection.

Most human scholars believe that Merfolk are the survivors of sunken Atlantis, humans adapted to the water. Merfolk, however, believe that humans sprang forth from Merfolk who adapted themselves in order to explore their last frontier.
These beings embody the essence of true heroes long dead. Summoned from the dreamrealms, they rise to meet their enemies.

"While, like a ghastly rapid river,
Through the pale door,
A hideous throng rush out forever,
And laugh—but smile no more."
—Edgar Allan Poe, "The Haunted Palace"
Occasionally a member of the Institute of Arcane Study acquires a taste for worldly pleasures. Seldom do they have trouble finding employment.
Legend has it that Serpents used to be bigger, but how could that be?
"This 'standing windstorm' can hold us off indefinitely? Ridiculous!" Saying nothing, she put a pinch of salt on the table. With a bang she clapped her hands, and the salt disappeared, blown away.
A deafening roar arose as the fury of an enormous vertical river supplanted our serenity. Eddies turned into whirling geysers, leveling everything in their path.

Unpredictable as the sea itself, Water Elementals shift without warning from tranquility to tempest. Capricious and fickle, they flow restlessly from one shape to another, expressing their moods with their physical forms.
Battle doesn't need a purpose; the battle is its own purpose. You don't ask why a plague spreads or a field burns. Don't ask why I fight.
'Twas in the bogs of Cannelbrae My mate did meet an early grave 'Twas nothing left for us to save In the peat-filled bogs of Cannelbrae.
Created to destroy Dominia, Demons can sometimes be bent to a more focused purpose.
Bones scattered around us joined to form misshapen bodies. We struck at them repeatedly—they fell, but soon formed again, with the same mocking look on their faceless skulls.

"There are some qualities—some incorporate things,/ That have a double life, which thus is made/ A type of twin entity which springs/ From matter and light, evinced in solid and shade."
—Edgar Allan Poe, "Silence"

"...There was no trace/ Of aught on that illumined face..."
—Samuel Coleridge, "Phantom"
The Nightmare arises from its lair in the swamps. As the poisoned land spreads, so does the Nightmare's rage and terrifying strength.

"Should you a Rat to madness tease
Why ev'n a Rat may plague you..."
—Samuel Coleridge, "Recantation"
Trained in the arts of stealth, the royal assassins choose their victims carefully, relying on timing and precision rather than brute force.

"They groaned, they stirred, they all uprose,/ Nor spake, nor moved their eyes;/ It had been strange, even in a dream,/ To have seen those dead men rise."/ —Samuel Coleridge, "The Rime of the Ancient Mariner"
The Wall of Bone is said to be an aspect of the Great Wall in Hel, where the bones of all sinners wait for Ragnarok, when Hela will call them forth for the final battle.

"About, about in reel and rout
The death-fires danced at night;
The water, like a witch's oils,
Burnt green, and blue and white."
—Samuel Coleridge, "The Rime of the Ancient Mariner"
They say the Zombie Master controlled these foul creatures even before his own death, but now that he is one of them, nothing can make them betray him.

"O to be a dragon . . . of silkworm size or immense . . ."
—Marianne Moore, "O to Be a Dragon"
Foolishly, Najib retreated to his castle at El-Abar; the next morning he was dead. In just one night, the dwarven forces had reduced the mighty walls to mere rubble.

Earth Elementals have the eternal strength of stone and the endurance of mountains. Primordially connected to the land they inhabit, they take a long-term view of things, scorning the impetuous haste of short-lived mortal creatures.

Fire Elementals are ruthless infernos, annihilating and consuming their foes in a frenzied holocaust. Crackling and blazing, they sear swift, terrible paths, leaving the land charred and scorched in their wake.

"And topples round the dreary west
A looming bastion fringed with fire."
—Alfred, Lord Tennyson, "In Memoriam"
"From up here we can drop rocks and arrows and more rocks!" "Uh, yeah boss, but how do we get down?"
To become king of the Goblins, one must assassinate the previous king. Thus, only the most foolish seek positions of leadership.

"While most overworlders fortunately don't realize this, Gargoyles can be most delicious, providing you have the appropriate tools to carve them."
—The Underworld Cookbook, by Asmoranomardicadaistinaculdacar

The Ogre philosopher Gnerdel believed the purpose of life was to live as high on the food chain as possible. She refused to eat vegetarians, and preferred to live entirely on creatures that preyed on sentient beings.
Fortunately, Hill Giants have large blind spots in which a human can easily hide. Unfortunately, these blind spots are beneath the bottoms of their feet.

The Minotaurs of the Hurloon Mountains are known for their love of battle. They are also known for their hymns to the dead, sung for friend and foe alike. These hymns can last for days, filling the mountain valleys with their low, haunting sounds.
Generations of genetic weeding have given rise to the deviously cowardly Ironclaw clan. To say that Orcs in general are vicious, depraved, and ignoble does not do justice to the Ironclaw.

The intricate dynamics of Rundvelt Goblin affairs are often confused with anarchy. The chaos, however, is the chaos of a thundercloud, and direction will sporadically and violently appear. Pashalik Mons and his raiders are the thunderhead that leads in the storm.
In a rare display of ingenuity, the Orcs invented an incredibly destructive weapon. Most Orcish artillerists are those who dared criticize its effectiveness.

We encountered a valley topped with immense boulders and eerie rock formations. Suddenly one of these boulders toppled from its perch and sprouted gargantuan wings, casting a shadow of darkness and sending us fleeing in terror.

The stench in the hovel was overpowering; something loathsome was cooking. Occasionally something surfaced in the thick paste, but my host would casually push it down before I could quite make out what it was.

While it's true most Dragons are cruel, the Shivan Dragon seems to take particular glee in the misery of others, often tormenting its victims much like a cat plays with a mouse before delivering the final blow.
What goes up, must come down.
None know if this Giant is the result of aberrant magics, Siamese twins, or a mentalist's schizophrenia.

"Oi oi oi, me gotta hurt in 'ere,
Oi oi oi, me smell a ting is near,
Gonna bosh 'n gonna nosh 'n da
hurt'll disappear."
—Traditional
Conjured from the bowels of hell, the fiery wall forms an impassable barrier, searing the soul of any creature attempting to pass through its terrible bursts of flame.

The Earth herself lends her strength to these walls of living stone, which possess the stability of ancient mountains. These mighty bulwarks thwart ground-based troops, providing welcome relief for weary warriors who defend the land.

The most terrifying thing about the Craw Wurm is probably the horrible crashing sound it makes as it speeds through the forest. This noise is so loud it echoes through the trees and seems to come from all directions at once.
I tell you, there was so many arrows flying about you couldn't hardly see the sun. So I says to young Angus, "Well, at least now we're fighting in the shade!"
Rather than sheltering her young, the female Fungusaur often injures her own offspring, thereby ensuring their rapid growth.
While it possesses potent venom, the Giant Spider often chooses not to paralyze its victims. Perhaps the creature enjoys the gentle rocking motion caused by its captives' struggles to escape its web.

Don't try to outrun one of Dominia's Grizzlies; it'll catch you, knock you down, and eat you. Of course, you could run up a tree. In that case you'll get a nice view before it knocks the tree down and eats you.

The mating habits of Treefolk, particularly the stalwart Ironroot Treefolk, are truly absurd. Molasses comes to mind. It's amazing the species can survive at all given such protracted periods of mate selection, conjugation, and gestation.
After years of training, the Druid becomes one with nature, drawing power from the land and returning it when needed.
Whenever the Llanowar Elves gather the fruits of their forest, they leave one plant of each type untouched, considering that nature's portion.
The only sound was the gentle clicking of the Faeries' wings. Then those intruders who were still standing turned and fled. One thing was certain: they didn't think the Scryb were very funny anymore.
Moving without sound, swift figures pass through branches and undergrowth completely unhindered. One with the trees around them, the Dryads of Shanodin Forest are seen only when they wish to be.
Moss-covered statues littered the area, a macabre monument to the Basilisk's power.
Though many think of Wolves as solitary predators, they are actually extremely social animals. During a hunt they often call to each other, which can be quite unsettling for their prey.
Some say magic was first practiced by women, who have always felt strong ties to the land.
"What else, when chaos draws all forces inward to shape a single leaf." —Conrad Aiken

"And through the drifts the snowy cliffs/ Did send a dismal sheen:/ Nor shapes of men nor beasts we ken—/ The ice was all between."/
—Samuel Coleridge, "The Rime of the Ancient Mariner"
Everybody knows that to ward off trouble, you knock on wood. But usually it's better to make a wall out of the wood and let trouble do the knocking.
I didn't think Mammoths could ever hold a candle to a well-trained battle horse. Then one day I turned my back on a drunken soldier. His blow never landed; Mi'cha flung the brute over ten meters.

"Some of the other guys dared me to touch it, but I knew it weren't no ordinary hunk o' rock."
—Norin the Wary
We had taken refuge in a small cave, thinking the entrance was too narrow for it to follow. To our horror, its gigantic head smashed into the mountainside, ripping itself a new entrance.

Some fiendish mage had created a horrifying wall of living flesh, patched together from a jumble of still-recognizable body parts. As we sought to hew our way through it, some unknown power healed the gaping wounds we cut, denying us passage.

"The foot stone is connected to the ankle stone, the ankle stone is connected to the leg stone..."
—Song of the Artificer
